question: Does exact evaluation of the same logged-action graph improve learning over constrained bootstrapping?

optimizer.loss: mean over states of mean SmoothL1 beta1 over each state's distinct recorded actions
optimizer.target: fixed float32 cast of backward float64 DP over logged edges only
optimizer.target_network: tau .01 maintained after each optimizer update; never queried by treatment optimizer

sampling.baseline_reconstruction: full30000 draws checked; same-budget prefix used in smoke
sampling.target_access: sampled current observations, observed-action masks and fixed logged-graph labels only

evaluation.action_selection: all four actions on fresh maps; no logged masks at deployment

recorded_actions.deduplication: state/action repeats must agree on reward, terminated, truncated and successor; no frequency weighting

logged_graph.absent_actions: NaN, excluded before max or loss
logged_graph.inputs: logged observed/reward/end/successor tables plus remaining clock and map identity; no exhaustive Q or world transition calls

fit_diagnostics.population: every supported current state, including states without a successful logged path
fit_diagnostics.prediction_order: saved sorted support rows; four online Q outputs per row
fit_diagnostics.state_errors: mean over states of mean observed-action absolute/squared error
fit_diagnostics.edge_errors: pooled observed-action absolute mean and maximum
fit_diagnostics.restricted_ranking: lowest-label predicted argmax within logged mask belongs to graph max set within atol1e-6 rtol0
fit_diagnostics.graph_regret: logged graph maximum minus graph value of predicted restricted argmax
